director.chapterArc: A progression from tactical observation to internal dread as the group's cohesion fractures under the weight of Rook's hidden agenda.
director.restraintNote: Maintain a grounded, analytical tone throughout. The horror is in the silence and the unspoken realization that Rook knows more than he says. Do not dramatize; let the facts land with heavy precision.

cues.delivery: Dessa's vulnerability is clinical and exhausted. She speaks of failure as a fact to be managed, not an emotional crisis.
cues.from: Dessa told him on the second night and made him promise before she told him.
cues.through: "Good." She put her boot back on, which took her some time and which she did entirely by herself. "That's the whole of the conversation and we're not having it again."
cues.reason: Shift from narrator observation to Dessa's intimate confession.

cues.delivery: Senna speaks with the weight of absolute certainty. Her voice is steady and protective, cutting through Toren's confusion.
cues.from: Senna said it on the fifth evening, to Toren, in the cart, with the rain off and the light going green over the ridge.
cues.through: "Ah," said Senna Voss. "Now that's the question, isn't it."
cues.reason: Shift to Senna's authoritative analysis of Rook.

cues.delivery: Wyck is flat and final. He speaks with the exhaustion of someone who has already processed a truth he cannot change.
cues.from: The thing with Wyck happened on the sixth evening and it took about nine seconds and it did not happen at all.
cues.through: "Go and do the water," he said.

cues.delivery: Milo asks the question with earnest fear; Rook's answer is a flat fact. The tension comes from the pause and the silence that follows.
cues.from: On the seventh night out of Coldharbour they camped in a half-collapsed field barn on the ridge with the whole of the country below them going dark, and Milo asked his question.
cues.through: Dessa noticed. Toren looked across the fire and found her already looking back at him, absolutely level, with her chin down, and she did not move a muscle of her face, and he understood perfectly.
cues.reason: Shift to Milo's inquiry and Rook's reluctant confirmation.

pauses.after: Especially when it was nothing. Toren heard him do it the whole way up.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the job of looking backward.
Emphasis on the repetition and failure.

pauses.after: "And nothing. Not one thing. Not a flicker of anything." She pressed her thumb in hard and her breath went out through her teeth. "And the awful part is that I can't even tell whether I'm doing it right, because the whole of doing it right was not doing nine things, and now there's a tenth thing, which is checking whether it's working."
pauses.reason: Emotional landing: Dessa's admission of failure and confusion.

pauses.after: "Good." She put her boot back on, which took her some time and which she did entirely by herself. "That's the whole of the conversation and we're not having it again."
pauses.reason: Scene transition from the conversation to the watch rota change.

pauses.after: "So a man like that does not take a road he cannot explain." She looked out at the green lane going north-east under the trees. "He's not running. I want you to understand that I have watched men run and this is not it, and I have watched men wander, and it is not that either." She said the rest of it quite gently. "That man is walking toward something. He's been walking toward it since before he came down off a bank into a rock cut, and he has picked up five people on the way, and he has not once turned round and gone back for any of them, which means he cannot."
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: Senna's revelation that Rook is walking toward a destination he cannot leave.
Brief pause for the impact of Wyck's single-word refusal.

pauses.before: then they know where people go
pauses.reason: The core realization about the book's purpose.

pauses.before: I'm not going to answer it tonight.
pauses.reason: Emphasis on the delay and withholding of truth.

pauses.after: It was not much. It was one word, and it was the shortest possible version of one word, and Rook had said no to that kind of question about eleven times in twenty days and had never once said anything else.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: The weight of Rook saying 'Yes' after so many refusals.
